title: Quantifying the energetics of molecular superbubbles in PHANGS galaxies
question: How can we resolve, identify, and characterise molecular superbubbles in nearby PHANGS galaxies to quantify stellar feedback energetics and constrain feedback models and efficiencies?

evidence.quote: We converted the CO luminosity into mass using a CO-to-H$_2$ factor ($\alpha_\text{CO}$) from (cite: sun_molecular_2020) which accounts for the mean variation of $\alpha_\text{CO}$ with galactocentric radius using a mass-metallicity relationship.

recipe.goal: Visually identify and kinematically confirm molecular superbubble candidates
recipe.method: Visual search across 60"x60" tiles (performed twice per galaxy) using stacked RGB images of ALMA CO T_peak (sqrt stretch), MUSE Halpha (log stretch), and HST B-band (linear stretch) for CO ring/partial-ring features with central/edge Halpha and HST sources. Candidates are verified in CO channel maps (>=3 channels persistence), horizontal/vertical PV diagrams (hole or arc expansion signatures), and radial velocity spectra to reject line-of-sight contamination.
key_parameters: Tile size ~60" x 60"; persistence >= 3 channels (~7.5 km s^-1); 25 candidates rejected via PV diagrams, leaving 325 bubbles
assumptions: Halpha emission limits detected single-burst bubble ages to <10 Myr

recipe.goal: Fit bubble centres and radii and classify sample via peer review
recipe.method: Visually draw circular apertures on the CO peak temperature (T_peak) shell ridge to measure bubble centres and radii R. Four team members then visually ranked all 325 candidates in CO into four categories (Closed Rings, Broken Rings, Dubious, Indeterminable), selecting the 88 Closed Rings as the fiducial sample. Fit power-law index to large radii using Pareto's MLE.
key_parameters: 4 categories: 1. Closed Rings (88), 2. Broken Rings (167), 3. Dubious (65), 4. Indeterminable (5); Pareto MLE power-law fit to radius distribution
assumptions: Bubble features are well characterised by circular apertures; shell thickness is unresolved so T_peak ridge traces radius

recipe.goal: Measure molecular shell mass, expansion velocity, and kinetic energy
recipe.method: Integrate CO luminosity within an aperture of 1.6R (based on the average radial T_peak profile) and convert to molecular shell mass M_sh using the radially varying alpha_CO from Sun et al. (2020). Measure receding and approaching velocities by hand from horizontal and vertical PV diagrams, apply spherical projection correction Eq. 1, and average the two directions to get v_exp. Compute kinetic energy as 0.5 * M_sh * v_exp^2.
key_parameters: Mass aperture = 1.6R (15% additional mass uncertainty); velocity measurement uncertainty = 3.0 km s^-1 (channel width 2.5 km s^-1)
assumptions: Spherical expansion geometry (valid since average bubble radius ~130 pc is smaller than 3x molecular scale height ~300 pc); galactocentric metallicity-dependent alpha_CO from Sun et al. (2020)

recipe.goal: Cross-match superbubbles with HST multi-scale stellar associations to derive stellar ages and masses
recipe.method: Assign PHANGS-HST V-band multi-scale stellar associations (at 16, 32, and 64 pc scales) overlapping the bubble radius R to each superbubble, excluding outliers with age > 15 Myr. Compute total stellar mass per bubble by summing association masses weighted by the fractional area overlapping the bubble radius (uncertainty via rms), and compute a single stellar age per bubble via mass-weighted mean (uncertainty via Eq. 2, replacing 0 Myr uncertainties with 0.5 Myr).
key_parameters: Association scales = 16, 32, 64 pc; age cutoff < 15 Myr; 0 Myr age uncertainty replaced with 0.5 Myr
assumptions: Single stellar population models from Bruzual & Charlot (2003) at solar metallicity, Chabrier (2003) IMF, and Cardelli et al. (1989) internal extinction used in CIGALE SED fitting

recipe.goal: Constrain expansion scaling law (eta), dynamical ages, feedback coupling efficiency (epsilon), and CO-derived cluster masses
recipe.method: Combine CO radii and expansion velocities with HST association ages in the self-similar thin-shell relation t_dyn = eta * R_s / v_s (Eq. 3) to measure the scaling constant eta. Adopt eta = 1/4 to compute CO dynamical ages t_dyn. Combine shell kinetic energy, t_dyn, Starburst99 mechanical luminosity per unit mass L, and HST stellar mass in Eq. 5 to solve for mechanical energy injection efficiency epsilon, and compute CO-derived cluster masses M_cl assuming epsilon = 10%.
key_parameters: gamma = 1 (radiative); eta = 1/4 adopted for t_dyn; L = 1 x 10^34 erg s^-1 M_sun^-1 (1 x 10^40 erg s^-1 per 10^6 M_sun); epsilon = 10% adopted for M_cl
assumptions: Self-similar thin-shell expansion with R_s = R and v_exp = v_ps = v_s (for radiative gamma = 1); dynamical age equals stellar population age; single dominant expansion mechanism; fully sampled Chabrier IMF at solar metallicity with constant mechanical luminosity per unit mass

recipe.goal: Estimate theoretical population of superbubbles and evaluate shell mass sweep-up
recipe.method: Estimate expected number of observable molecular superbubbles using Clarke & Oey (2002) Eq. 17 from average galaxy SFR in ALMA FoV, mean CO-derived cluster mass, mean bubble lifetime, and a 30% bubble merger fraction. Evaluate shell mass sweep-up by comparing stellar-to-shell mass ratios against a 1% star formation efficiency reference line as a function of bubble radius and age, and fitting shell mass increase between R = 100 and 200 pc.
key_parameters: Mean CO-derived cluster mass = 4.8 x 10^5 M_sun; mean bubble lifetime = 3.6 Myr; average SFR in ALMA FoV = 2.5 M_sun yr^-1; bubble merger fraction = 30%; baseline SFE = 1%; ambient density = 50 cm^-3; molecular scale height = 100 pc
assumptions: Instantaneous star formation efficiency of 1%; negligible cluster mass loss from stellar ejections or winds/SNe

evidence.quote: We visually find 325 cavities across 18 PHANGS–ALMA galaxies, 88 of which have clear superbubble signatures (unbroken shells, central clusters, kinematic signatures of expansion).

score_reason: High-level PHANGS-ALMA v1.0 data products are public and the authors publicly release the complete machine-readable tables of measured bubble coordinates, radii, velocities, shell masses, and cross-matched HST stellar association properties on CANFAR (allowing exact reproduction of all downstream energetic calculations), though the initial visual search, manual circular aperture fitting, and by-hand PV velocity measurements are inherently human-driven and rely on internal v1.3 HST catalogues.
rediscovery_reason: The PHANGS-ALMA v1.0 data cubes/maps and the authors' complete catalogue of 88 superbubbles (including coordinates, radii, velocities, masses, and HST association properties on CANFAR) are publicly available, and the main results (radius distribution slope, shell masses, expansion velocities, dynamical scaling parameter eta, and ~10% SN feedback coupling efficiency) are well-defined quantitative metrics.
